mathematical_findings: Injection of the retained vertex set makes the restriction unique. The intertwining calculation proves multiplicativity; pointwise rigidity and extension existence give the isomorphism and its distinguished subgroup image.
Component boundaries distinguish local pieces without assuming that a correlation already fixes their palettes. The induced coloring restriction is explained.
Chamber completion covers every clique, including empty and singleton cases. Old degree d(v)(r-1) is strictly larger than the new degree r-1, also with r=2 and no new vertices.
Cleaning counts both new palettes correctly and recognizes the old set by color-class sizes. Common neighbors reconstruct deleted old edges. Gadget boundaries are distinct pairs or singletons.
The cleaning tail rigidity handles M=1 and isolated attachments: the root is intrinsically fixed; internal degrees distinguish both branch choices even when u2 has an extra old neighbor.

The ordered-pair graph recognizes old vertices even at q=2. Degree-two old neighbors identify T, terminal degree-three vertices identify the target, and the unique internal chain recovers the ordered label.

Full uncolored automorphisms are right translations; using g inverse gives the correct composition homomorphism. Normality of H is explicitly used to permute every coset color and identify the color kernel.
The encoder vertex count sums q(k+4) internal vertices per label plus q originals. Connectedness is supplied by this encoder rather than attributed to cleaning of disconnected inputs.

The symmetric recursion has a genuine degree-one n=2 base; n=3 and all later degrees are treated separately. Even coset representatives give compatible parity permutations and the displayed cocycle composition.

For n=3, degrees distinguish the top class despite equal palette sizes. The proof that X_m minus its top is connected supplies component recognition after removing the new top and pair vertices. Distinct boundary stars then give full correlation rigidity.

The hexagon example proves the full corrected pair (D12,S3), not merely a lower bound from the displayed involution. The initial graph has triangles and is explicitly outside chamber-completion hypotheses.
Source authorship and exact three corrections are retained. Source Question2.4 was answered by its own theorem; no new conjecture credit or graph optimality assertion is made.
